about.title: San Anselmo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Anselmo is a small town of about 12,653 people, and a sudden loss here tends to ripple through neighbors, schools, and the shops along San Anselmo Avenue. Public records for 2025 show 29 injury collisions and 36 people hurt within city limits, with no traffic deaths recorded that year; Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Center Boulevard, Butterfield Road, and San Anselmo Avenue carried the highest collision counts, and reports clustered on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Yet wrongful death claims in Marin County arise from far more than roadway crashes. A missed diagnosis, a fall on poorly kept property, a defective product, or an incident at work can each leave a family facing funeral bills and a household budget that no longer balances. Under California law, a wrongful death case is a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges, and only certain relatives may bring it. Our team reviews what happened and explains your options, free of charge.

whyChoose.title: Why San Anselmo Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can confirm where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting started promptly keeps those dates from slipping by while you grieve.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency. Funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance can all be pursued without paying up front.

items.question: My relative was killed in a crash on Sir Francis Drake Boulevard and the driver was cited. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, a criminal citation or charge and a wrongful death claim are two separate tracks. The criminal case is brought by the state and does not compensate your family for funeral costs or lost support. A civil wrongful death action is how relatives recover those losses, and it proceeds whether or not the driver is ever convicted.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the decedent's children have first priority. If there are none, certain dependents and other heirs may qualify under California law. Because standing rules are strict, we usually sort this out at the very first conversation.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Marin County?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death. If a public agency such as a city, county, or transit district may share fault, a formal claim typically has to be presented within six months. Reaching out sooner rather than later protects every option your family may have.
